audit.why: 50.38% over 1975 games, rated 8/10 hard. The difficulty is Wind Wall (25/23/21/19/17s, 4 seconds, blocks all projectiles) deleting your Q in both directions, plus Sweeping Blade's 0.5s cooldown turning any wave into a staircase. What keeps it playable is range: Steel Tempest is 475 against your 900 Q.
audit.corrected: 8/10 retained, expressed through the two numbers that cause it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 and late-game text described his ultimate only as 'knock-up-reliant' without the numbers or the condition, and never mentioned that Last Breath drops from 70s to 30s.
audit.why: Last Breath is 70/50/30 and blinks 1400 to an Airborne enemy champion. That makes level 6 a fight about denying the second Steel Tempest stack, and makes the late game a fight about nobody on your side being knocked up — a very different instruction from 'dodge his all-in'.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, spikes[3].text, late and breakdown.late rebuilt on the airborne condition and the 70s/30s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere stated that Wind Wall blocks the Q RECAST as well as the cast, that Steel Tempest's knock-up needs two stacks, that Sweeping Blade needs a target unit to dash to, or that Way of the Wanderer shields him when he takes damage.
audit.why: Aurora's Q is flagged projectile and the recast draws the curse back through the same space, so a wall that eats the throw eats the return too — that is the single most important interaction in the lane and it was unwritten. Sweeping Blade dashes through a target enemy on a 0.5s cooldown, so wave state controls his access to you. The passive shield means the front of your burst lands on a shield, not health.
audit.corrected: report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d, wants.foe[0], breakdown.wave and breakdown.feeding now carry these.

audit.why: Defect item 3. Wind Wall 25s at rank 1 for 4 seconds, Steel Tempest 4s, Sweeping Blade 0.5s, Last Breath 70/50/30.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the numbers that decide when to throw a Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cross-layer chart disagreement on all seven rows: every phases[N].side read 'Yasuo' while win[0..6] all read 'Aurora' and the packet levelChart reads Aurora on all seven.
audit.why: Packet and content agree, and every phases[N].why already describes Aurora spiking, so the side token was the lone dissenter and contradicted the sentence printed beneath it. Kit support: he has to enter 475 to do anything, and she pokes from 900.
audit.corrected: All seven sides set to Aurora as one group. Ratings and whys left as they stand — they already state the Aurora verdict.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Check it before every step-up. - W Across the Veil is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1 for 4 seconds of cover, and it eats your Q in both directions. - Steel Tempest is a 4s cooldown, so the knock-up is never far away. - Last Breath is 70s at rank 1 and only fires at an airborne target.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by walling your Q, stacking Steel Tempest into a knock-up, and blinking 1400 with Last Breath onto it.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-recast cleared push that crashes on your trade timers — your patterns farm and poke in the same cast. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with W down — hop-less Aurora is a skinny mage with a haste passive and regrets. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.
edits.after: Best wave: keep it shoved — Sweeping Blade needs a target to dash to, and a wave sitting on your side is a free ladder to your face. Worst wave: a big crashed wave in the middle, where he chains E through six minions and arrives with two Tempest stacks. Crash timing: crash, then step back to 900 and hold the wave thin.

edits.before: If Yasuo gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Wind Wall extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q recasts and stay relevant through zone utility.
edits.after: A fed Yasuo buys crit and his passive shield holds through your opener, so the burst you counted on arrives short. Behind, farm at 900 and never stand next to a minion he can dash to.

edits.before: Carry through tempo — patterns that exit free compound; your zone turns objective fights into speed checks they fail.
edits.after: Carry by never being reachable: he needs a target for Sweeping Blade and an airborne one for Last Breath — give him neither.

edits.before: You warp the fight: R the clump, hop through the middle, and pattern whoever the zone slows. The exit portal is your insurance.
edits.after: Late, Last Breath is 30s and he only needs one of you knocked up — stay spread, keep E for his landing, and R away from the clump.

edits.before: Ahead, pace the lane: pattern Yasuo off every contact, hop his answers, and drop R on each river fight — the zone converts leads into routs.
edits.after: Ahead, keep the wave off him: shove, poke on the 25s Wind Wall gap, and take fights where he has no minion to dash through to reach you.

edits.before: Track Yasuo’s Wind Wall: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Wind Wall blocks your Q for 4 seconds on a 25s cooldown, and it blocks the recast too. Steel Tempest knocks up on its second stack.

edits.before: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade dashes through minions on a near-zero cooldown, so slow the chain with E as he arrives rather than after.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E the step-up, Q-recast the slowed target, hop out — a full pattern he answered with a whiff.
edits.after: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 and lasts 4 — throw the Q after it expires, not into a wall that eats both halves.

edits.before: Yasuo spends Wind Wall early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Two Steel Tempest stacks means the third cast knocks up — hop that, not the poke.

edits.before: That is Yasuo’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Inside 475 he stacks Steel Tempest on you every 4 seconds.

edits.before: W spent as an entrance is W unavailable as an exit — the whole kit's promise breaks on that one greed.
edits.after: W is 22s and E is 15s at rank 1 — burn both in one trade and his next dash finds you standing still.

edits.before: Hopping IN with W and trading while his engage is still loaded — the exit spent as an entrance is how Auroras get coached postmortem.
edits.after: With Between Worlds on cooldown you have no slow field to break his dash chain — fight where minions are thin so Sweeping Blade has no targets.

edits.before: Your Q Twin Drift poke keeps Yasuo off balance since he needs to walk into your range to get value from Steel Tempest, and E The Weirding punishes any wave-clear attempt with Wind Wall down.
edits.after: Steel Tempest only reaches 475, so every stack he wants costs him a walk into your 900 Q — and with Wind Wall on its 25s he has no answer to the recast coming back through him.

edits.before: His Last Breath knock-up threat requires a knock-up setup first, and Between Worlds lets you avoid getting caught out by his all-in the moment he commits to a dash.
edits.after: Last Breath is 70s at rank 1 and only blinks to an airborne target, so denying the second Steel Tempest stack denies the ultimate — that is the whole level 6 fight.

edits.before: Your kiting and burst still outclass his all-in dive potential since Between Worlds gives you an escape from his gap-close tools even once he's fully itemized.
edits.after: Late he blinks 1400 with Last Breath and crits through armour, so the answer is distance: E on his landing, W out, and never be the airborne one.

edits.before: You control the level 1-2 lane phase since Yasuo has to walk into melee range to threaten you, letting your Q Twin Drift poke punish every approach attempt without much risk.
edits.after: You control levels 1-2 because Steel Tempest is 475 and Sweeping Blade needs a minion to arrive on — poke him at 900 and keep the wave from becoming his staircase.

edits.before: Through levels 3 to 6 you maintain the lead as his all-in still requires a landed knock-up to be safe, and your Between Worlds dodge tool means his ultimate arrival doesn't create the guaranteed kill window he wants.
edits.after: Through levels 3 to 6 you keep the lead because his all-in needs two Steel Tempest stacks first, and your E slows the dash chain that stacks them. Wind Wall is 25s, so the poke window comes back before his does.

edits.before: You keep the edge into the late game and beyond because your escape and burst combo continues to outpace his all-in potential, letting you punish his engages even as he scales into a stronger crit-based build.
edits.after: You keep the edge late because his ultimate still needs someone airborne: Last Breath is 30s at rank 3 but it blinks only to a knocked-up target, so spread out, hold E for his landing, and his crit build never gets the opening.

edits.before: Poke from range and punish his dash cooldown windows before he closes distance
edits.after: Poke at 900 and punish him when no minion is left to dash through to you

edits.before: Wind Wall your key poke or burst spell to neutralize your damage window
edits.after: Wind Wall your Q so that both the cast and the recast hit nothing

notes: 1) The packet's suspect name 'His Last Breath' is a FALSE POSITIVE — Last Breath is Yasuo's real R. The sentence was still wrong for other reasons (no cooldown, no airborne condition) and was rewritten. 2) I did NOT claim Aurora's E passes through Wind Wall. Her E carries no projectile flag in the kit, but wall eligibility is exactly the class of fact Riot's text does not state, so it stays unverified — I wrote only that the Q (flagged projectile, and drawn back through the same space on recast) is blocked both ways. If someone can confirm whether Wind Wall stops The Weirding, that single fact would upgrade this matchup's advice materially. 3) 'Q Twin Drift' recurs in spikes[0].text and early; unverifiable from the brief, so removed rather than guessed. Note that the same sentence names Aurora's E 'The Weirding', which suggests the content author had a name source — worth checking both against the kit file. 4) All seven phases[].side rows read 'Yasuo' against a packet and content chart of Aurora on all seven, with Aurora-positive whys printed underneath. Flipped as one group. 5) Worth a second look independently of this audit: the matchup is labelled HARD 8/10 at a 50.38% win rate with an all-Aurora level chart. The three do not obviously sit together, but I had no kit basis to change diff or diffRating, so I left them.
